narration.text: Try not to yawn while you watch this.
Too late? Just reading the word yawn can set some people off.
It's not about oxygen. When people breathed pure oxygen in a lab, they yawned just as much.
One leading idea: yawning cools your brain. That big gulp of air helps cool the blood heading to your head.
Animals with bigger brains yawn longer. A mouse yawns for under a second. You, about six.
And yawns spread. Roughly half of adults catch one just from seeing someone else yawn.
You catch them faster from family and friends than from strangers.
Young kids rarely catch yawns until about age four or five.
And babies already yawn in the womb.
So, how many times did you yawn? Be honest.
